terms.label: Layer
terms.meaning: A part of an ordered arrangement in which each part depends only on the parts beneath it, the standard technical sense (the OSI model, a layered software architecture). Whether a part is a layer depends on the whole arrangement, so the test runs on the whole: its dependencies hold no cycle and put every part in one stack, and beneath means depended on. The ontology's three layers pass. Naive's groupings fail, both the seven EE-001 decided (a loop) and the seven manifests as built (their reads form cycles), so for them "layer" is the system's name for its parts, not this term.

properties.says: an arrangement of at least two parts
no part depends on itself, directly or through other parts (no cycle)
one stack: of any two parts, one depends on the other, directly or through other parts

sources: ISO/IEC 7498-1:1994, the OSI basic reference model
Buschmann et al., Pattern-Oriented Software Architecture, vol. 1 (1996), the Layers pattern
Dijkstra, The structure of the THE multiprogramming system (1968)
Ledger N-096 and C-086 (2026-10-31): layer reserved for the technical sense

terms.label: Area
terms.meaning: A part of an arrangement drawn around one concern, with nothing required of the order among the parts: dependencies may run any way, loops included. The contrast to layer, and the word C-086 proposed for Naive's groupings. A layer need not be an area, and an area need not be a layer.

properties.says: an arrangement of at least two parts
each part drawn around one concern

sources: Dijkstra, On the role of scientific thought (EWD447, 1974): separation of concerns
Parnas, On the criteria to be used in decomposing systems into modules (1972)
Ledger C-086 (2026-10-31): Naive's groupings proposed as areas

terms.label: Top category
terms.meaning: A category at the top of a hierarchy of categories joined by broader links, as in an upper ontology. Whether a category is a top category depends on the whole hierarchy, so the test runs on the whole: broader holds no cycle, a top category has nothing broader, every other category has something broader, and none reaches two top categories. packages/naive/lean/Naive/Upper.lean proves that on any finite hierarchy no cycle, no orphan and no category reaching two top categories give every category exactly one top category (upper_one_top_of_checks); that these checks state those hypotheses is read off the code, not proved. Naive's top categories are listed in packages/naive/src/terms/ontology.json, each mapped to a class of BFO (N-049).

properties.says: no category is broader than itself, directly or through others (no cycle)
a top category has nothing broader
every category that is not a top category has something broader (no orphan)
no category reaches two top categories

sources: ISO/IEC 21838-2:2021, Basic Formal Ontology
W3C SKOS Reference (2009): skos:broader, skos:hasTopConcept
Ledger N-049 (2026-11-02): own top categories, each mapped to BFO; every noun traces to exactly one through broader
docs/design/ONTOLOGY_CORE_2026-11-04.md, part 2

terms.label: Typed link
terms.meaning: A link from one record to another whose type names how they relate, drawn from a closed set of standard relations: between ideas, broader, narrower, related, part-of, derived-from, builds_on, supports and contradicts; from an idea to its scope, creates, amends, appends_to and derives_from (packages/naive/src/terms/relations.ts, each mapped to SKOS, PROV-O, DCMI Terms, AIF and IBIS). Whether a link is well typed depends on the whole graph, since an ordering relation must not close a cycle, so the test runs on the whole: every type is in the closed set for its target, no idea links to itself, every target exists (a scope the idea creates may be new), and no cycle runs through broader (narrower read backwards), part-of or builds_on.

properties.says: every link's type is in the closed set for its target: an idea relation to an idea, a scope attachment to a scope
no idea links to itself
every link names a target that exists, except a scope the idea creates
no cycle runs through broader (narrower read backwards), part-of or builds_on

sources: Trigg, A Network-Based Approach to Text Handling for the Online Scientific Community (1983): typed links
W3C SKOS Reference (2009): broader, narrower, related
W3C PROV-O (2013): wasDerivedFrom
DCMI Metadata Terms: isPartOf, source, requires, relation
Chesnevar et al., Towards an argument interchange format (2006): inference and conflict nodes
Kunz and Rittel, Issues as elements of information systems (1970); Conklin and Begeman, gIBIS (1988): supports, objects-to, specializes, generalizes
Preserved PR 157 (EE-103): the noun relations broader, narrower, related, part-of and derived-from
